drafted_from: tool:find-music-windows-that-follow-a-loudness-arc row in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/tool-rows.json, its script in tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/ and tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (run for real on made-up tones)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the 10 second stretch of /work/music/track.wav whose loudness follows my film's arc in BRIEF.json and cut it as an excerpt." It runs the window finder and reads which window won.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads BRIEF.json and music tracks on this computer and writes windows.json and excerpt files into the folder it is given.
instructions: 1. Write /work/music/brief.json with arc [[seconds, dB], ...], length_s, and the measured constraints open, lift and swell as [start, end] seconds.

2. Say "Find the music windows". The AI reads the row with tools:list and runs: python3 -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/find_music_windows.py /work/music/brief.json /work/music/out /work/music/track.wav (name more tracks after it).
3. Read the last line, then open out/music/windows.json: each window has start_s, end_s, arc_score, corr, open_db, lift_db, swell_db and the excerpt path in out/music/excerpts/.
4. Run tool:listen-to-music-windows-against-a-film-brief on the same folder to judge the excerpts by ear.

worked_examples.title: A 40 s track with a loud swell at 25 s: the 10 s window starting at 19 s follows the arc
worked_examples.ask: Find the stretch of this track that follows my film's loudness arc.
worked_examples.given: From tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/test/test_judge_sound_effects.py (test_the_window_that_follows_the_arc_wins_and_is_listened_to, run for real): track.wav is 40 s of a 220 Hz tone with loudness 0.02 until 20 s, rising to 0.4 at 25 s, falling to 0.05 by 30 s; brief.json has arc [[0, -12], [5, 0], [10, -6]], length_s 10, open [0, 2], lift [4, 6], swell [4, 6]. Command: python3 -I tools/generate-and-judge-sound-effects/do-work/find_music_windows.py /work/music/brief.json /work/music/out /work/music/track.wav
worked_examples.hands_back: Last line: {"result": {"windows": "/work/music/out/music/windows.json", "tracks": 1}}. windows.json has hop_s 0.25 and one window for track: start_s 19.0, end_s 29.0, arc_score 1.119, corr 0.971, open_db -31.8, lift_db -13.2, swell_db -11.9, excerpt /work/music/out/music/excerpts/{track}@{19}.wav (the track name, @ and the start second, as find_music_windows.py names it).
